title: Recursive Viability
hook: If everything in your business stops when you take a week off, you built a job.
statement: Organize your business and life into parts that can run on their own and still stay in sync.
explainer: When you're the hub for every decision, you become the bottleneck. Parts that run solo but still coordinate let you step back without things falling apart.
sop: List the parts of your business or life: departments, roles, routines.
Score Autonomy and Coordination from 1 to 10 for each.
Hand off one full routine with real decision power, not just tasks.
Set up a simple weekly sync so you're not the connector.
Step back for a week and see what breaks.
equation_example: Part one: Autonomy 7 × Coordination 6 = 42. Part two: Autonomy 5 × Coordination 8 = 40. Add them: 42 + 40 = 82. Higher means things run without you and stay in sync. Lower means everything needs you, or nothing talks.
question: Write down which part of your business would break first if you disappeared for a week.
closing_statement: Build parts that work alone and still work together.
caption:
Principle Nº 192: Recursive Viability

If everything in your business stops when you take a week off, you built a job.

Organize your business and life into parts that can run on their own and still stay in sync.

Your turn: Write down which part of your business would break first if you disappeared for a week.
